name: Dizi
confidence_why: The only statement on Dizi stress is Beachy 2005 reporting Breeze 1988 that stress is non-contrastive and "generally" falls on the first syllable, with Beachy adding that this needs further research, while Allan 1976 says nothing about stress and describes Dizi as a three-level tone language, so initial stress is a plausible but unconfirmed reading.
catalog_quote: Breeze found that stress was not contrastive in Dizin or Benchnon "but generally falls on the first syllable of a word" (1988:482). This needs to be researched further.
readall_conflicts: No disagreement between sources on stress, because only one direct stress statement exists and it is secondhand: Beachy 2005 (already held by the project at, printed p. 47 = p. 64, section 2.6 'Stress') reports that Breeze (1988:482) found stress not contrastive in Dizin or Benchnon 'but generally falls on the first syllable of a word', and adds 'This needs to be researched further.' That is the whole basis of the catalog's fixed: initial syllable rule. Allan 1976, the only listed work opened, is silent on stress and describes Dizi as a three-level register tone language in which lexical tone is marginal and grammatical tone (possession, verb tense/aspect classes) is central. Nothing opened contradicts the initial-stress record, but nothing opened confirms it either, and Seyoum 2021 (the most likely modern statement) could not be downloaded.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: confirmed verbatim in the Beachy 2005 PDF we hold at printed p.47, section 2.6. (2) The classification 'fixed-strict initial, in the dominant set' rests on a single second-hand sentence: Beachy 2005 (MA thesis) quoting Breeze 1988:482 that stress is non-contrastive and 'generally' initial, immediately followed by Beachy's own 'This needs to be researched further'; Dizin is analysed by all sources as a three-level tone language, and Beachy p.56 again flags stress as uninvestigated. Nothing found contradicts initial stress, but 'generally' plus the explicit hedge makes 'strict' stronger than the source; the evidence is thin rather than wrong. (3) Better/primary sources exist but are not yet obtained: Breeze 1988 itself (print only), Seyoum 2021 phonology article (RG author upload, could not be reached by automated download
